issues.description: Inner blocking read loop removes timeout and process-exit safety nets, trading truncation for potential deadlock.
issues.detail: Once O_NONBLOCK is cleared, the new while-True os.read() has no poll timeout and no check_process_exited backstop. If the writer hangs without closing the FIFO (or an inherited fd holds the write end in a grandchild), the parent blocks forever. The original loop's invariant must be preserved on the drain path.

issues.description: fcntl mode switch lacks error handling and try/finally; fd left in inconsistent blocking state on exception.
issues.detail: F_GETFL/F_SETFL can raise OSError, and any exception in the inner read loop leaves the fd in blocking mode for whoever inherits it. There is no try/finally restoring flags and no documented pre/post-condition. Wrap the mode change with error handling and guaranteed cleanup.

issues.description: Patch silently deletes the macOS EOF workaround and drops has_blocking_error semantics in one diff.
issues.detail: The removed block existed because POSIX EOF behavior wasn't observed on macOS FIFOs; the commit asserts POSIX guarantees without proof. Simultaneously, has_blocking_error tracking is replaced by a bare pass. Either justify subsumption with evidence or split into separate patches so behavior change is reviewable.

issues.description: No regression test for the intermittent 86KB truncation race.
issues.detail: A race fix without a deterministic test will regress on the next refactor. A fixture that writes a >64KB payload then exits immediately would exercise both the wait-for-first-byte and drain-to-EOF phases. Add a test before merging.

issues.description: Two read loops with different EOF semantics complect the protocol; extract drain as a named function.
issues.detail: The function now runs a non-blocking outer loop and a blocking inner loop, each with its own EOF logic and nested break-break control flow. Decompose into wait_for_first_byte and drain_blocking(fifo_fd) -> bytes. This both clarifies the phases and exposes a unit-testable surface.

issues.description: Root cause is unframed IPC; the real fix belongs on the writer side.
issues.detail: The writer subprocess emits an unframed JSON blob and relies on EOF for termination, making liveness load-bearing in the reader. A length-prefixed or newline-delimited frame on the writer would make the reader trivial and eliminate the race class entirely. Worth naming even if this reader-side patch ships.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the diagnosis (non-blocking read race against kernel pipe buffering) is correct and the two-phase strategy is sound in shape, but execution is unsafe. The blocking drain loop discards the original timeout and process-exit safeguards, so an intermittent truncation has been traded for a possible indefinite hang. The fcntl mode switch lacks error handling and cleanup, and the patch bundles a silent removal of the macOS workaround with a drop of has_blocking_error semantics. No regression test accompanies a concurrency fix. Recommend: keep a timeout/process-exit backstop on the blocking path, guard the fd mode change with try/finally, justify or restore the macOS handling, and add a deterministic >64KB test before merge.
